cases.reason: Check 3: step 1 'Click "Cancel order", then press Esc' and step 2 'Click "Cancel order" again, then click outside' each hold two actions, and the steps do not say on which page. Check 2: 'The confirmation closes' on Esc / outside click is not in spec.yaml; REQ-SCRUM-9-14 only requires that the order stays unchanged.
cases.suggestion: Split into: open My Orders; click "Cancel order" (confirmation opens); press Esc (order still Received); and the same for a click outside. Expect only what the spec requires: the order is not cancelled (still Received after reload); record whether the dialog closes as an observation, not a pass criterion.
Optional: add the tag REQ-SCRUM-9-01 (it is in the description but not in the tags).

cases.reason: Check 3: step 2 'Click "Cancel order", then "Cancel order" in the confirmation' holds two actions, and the confirmation opening has no expected result of its own.
cases.suggestion: Split step 2 into: click "Cancel order" (the confirmation opens) and click "Cancel order" in the confirmation (status title "Cancelled").

cases.reason: Check 2: step 2 expects 'no current or completed step of the order progress'. REQ-SCRUM-9-18 only says the bar 'does not show a cancelled order as in progress'; the test basis does not say whether an already completed step (for example Received) may still be shown, so the stricter expectation cannot be confirmed from spec.yaml.
cases.suggestion: Ask the product owner what the progress bar must show for a cancelled order, or reduce the expected result to the spec wording (the bar does not show the order as in progress).

cases.reason: Check 5: the case traces only to REQ-SCRUM-9-12, for which plan §4 sets 'State transition (button per status)', but the case uses 'decision table (owner = yes, status = Accepted)'. Also it checks only Accepted on the tracking page; Delivered and Declined are not checked there.
cases.suggestion: Either label it state transition (button per status) and add steps for Delivered and Declined orders on the tracking page, or add REQ-SCRUM-9-11 to its traceability (the decision-table row signed in = yes, owner = yes, status = Accepted).
REQ-SCRUM-9-20 also requires its own colour in the order details; step 1 checks only the spelling. Consider adding the colour check (see missing test cases).

cases.reason: Check 3: step 2 'As customer A, place an order and cancel it on My Orders' holds several actions in two applications; the order total is never noted, so step 3 'does not include the cancelled order's total' cannot be checked.
cases.suggestion: Split step 2 into: place a takeaway order and note its number and total (T); on My Orders cancel it (shows "Cancelled"). In step 3 compare the figure with R1 and T.

cases.reason: Check 3: step 2 'As customer A, place an order; as admin, decline it' holds two actions by two users; the expected result 'The order shows Declined' does not say where; the order total is never noted, so step 3 cannot be checked.
cases.suggestion: Split step 2 into: as A place an order and note its number and total (T); as admin decline it (admin list shows Declined). Compare the figure in step 3 with R1 and T.

Note: 'Accept and Reject actions are offered' for a Received order is inferred from REQ-SCRUM-9-23, not stated in spec.yaml; the spec-based part is that the status can still be changed and Cancelled is not offered.

cases.reason: Check 3: step 2 'Open a chef, add a dish to the cart and place a takeaway order' holds three actions; step 4 'Click "Cancel order", then "Cancel order" in the confirmation' holds two and the confirmation has no expected result of its own. cases.suggestion: Split steps 2 and 4 into single actions, each with its own expected result. Keep the layout remark as an observation or tie it to a stated requirement.
